info.title: JobsNow APIs used by the front end
info.description: Merge of the OpenAPI documents of the js API (login, port 8082) and of the jn API (asynchronous tasks, port 8080). Each path carries the server of its API.

tags.name: Login
tags.description: Login controls for token and password registration, pre-registration, and various lock management flows such as: token lock, password lock, and token unlock requests.

tags.name: AsyncTask
tags.description: Asynchronous tasks — operations executed in the background whose result can be polled by ID.

post.description:
When does it occur? Right after the user types their password. What does it do? Authenticates the user and generates a session token to be used in subsequent authenticated requests. The optional query parameter wordsHash can be sent by the frontend: if it matches the backend value, the word list is not returned. Otherwise, the full word list and its new hash are returned and must be stored in application storage (long-term browser storage).

Request body fields (JSON):
  • userAgent – Required. Must be a non-empty string.
  • ip – Required. String, min 7 / max 45 characters (IPv4 or IPv6 address of the client).
  • email – Required. Valid email address. Min 7, max 100 characters.
  • password – Required. Strong password: minimum 8 characters, at least 1 uppercase letter, 1 lowercase letter, 1 digit, and 1 special character.

400.description: Invalid email format. The frontend should display a generic system error.

200.description: User logged in successfully. The frontend should dismiss the login modal and store the 'sessionToken' returned in the JSON.

427.description: Wrong password entered. Still within the allowed attempt limit. The frontend should display an error message with the remaining attempt count.

423.description: Password pending unlock. The frontend should redirect the user to the password change screen.

201.description: Pre-registration data is pending. The frontend should redirect the user to the pre-registration screen.

429.description: Password just locked — maximum wrong attempts exceeded. The frontend should redirect the user to the password re-registration screen.

202.description: Password registration is pending. The frontend should redirect the user to the password registration screen.

403.description: Token is locked. The frontend should redirect the user to the token unlock request screen.

409.description: User already logged in. The frontend should redirect the user to the password change screen.

404.description: New user — email not found in the system. The frontend should redirect the user to the email confirmation screen.

post.description:
When does it occur? Right after confirming it is the user's first access and they have confirmed their email. What does it do? Sends a token to the user's email so they can use it to register a password.

Request body fields (JSON):
  • userAgent – Required. Must be a non-empty string.
  • ip – Required. String, min 7 / max 45 characters (IPv4 or IPv6 address of the client).
  • email – Required. Valid email address. Min 7, max 100 characters.

400.description: Invalid email format. The frontend should display a generic system error.

409.description: User already logged in. The frontend should redirect the user to the password change screen.

200.description: Password already registered, user has no pending registrations. The frontend should redirect the user to the password entry screen.

403.description: Token is locked. The frontend should redirect the user to the token unlock request screen.

423.description: Password pending unlock. The frontend should redirect the user to the password change screen.

202.description: Token for password registration sent to user's email. The frontend should redirect the user to the password registration screen.

201.description: Pre-registration is pending. The frontend should redirect the user to the pre-registration screen.

head.description:
When does it occur? Right after the user shows interest in accessing authenticated resources. What does it do? Checks whether the user exists and whether there are any pending registration steps (password, pre-registration).

Request body fields (JSON):
  • userAgent – Required. Must be a non-empty string.
  • ip – Required. String, min 7 / max 45 characters (IPv4 or IPv6 address of the client).
  • email – Required. Valid email address. Min 7, max 100 characters.

400.description: Invalid email format. The frontend should display a generic system error.

404.description: New user — email not found. The frontend should redirect the user to the email confirmation screen.

200.description: Password registered, no pending registrations. The frontend should redirect the user to the password entry screen.

202.description: Password registration is pending. The frontend should redirect the user to the password registration screen.

423.description: Password pending unlock. The frontend should redirect the user to the password change screen.

403.description: Token is locked. The frontend should redirect the user to the token unlock request screen.

201.description: Pre-registration is pending. The frontend should redirect the user to the pre-registration screen.

409.description: User already logged in. The frontend should redirect the user to the password change screen.

post.description:
When does it occur? When the user needs to unlock a previously locked token. What does it do? Registers an unlock request for the locked token so a support bot can process it.

Request body fields (JSON):
  • userAgent – Required. Must be a non-empty string.
  • ip – Required. String, min 7 / max 45 characters (IPv4 or IPv6 address of the client).
  • email – Required. Valid email address. Min 7, max 100 characters.

404.description: Token is not locked — unlock is not applicable.

429.description: Token already unlocked or already resent.

post.description:
When does it occur? When the user's token is locked due to too many wrong attempts and they want a new token. What does it do? Registers a resend request for the locked token so a support bot can process it.

Request body fields (JSON):
  • userAgent – Required. Must be a non-empty string.
  • ip – Required. String, min 7 / max 45 characters (IPv4 or IPv6 address of the client).
  • email – Required. Valid email address. Min 7, max 100 characters.

409.description: Resend or unlock request already submitted.

429.description: Token has already been resent or unlocked.

404.description: Token is not locked — resend is not applicable.

post.summary: Request login token by email with language preference
post.description:
When does it occur? When the user needs a token and wants to receive the email in a specific language. What does it do? Sends a token to the user's email in the requested language so they can register a password.

Path variables:
  • language – Required. Accepted values: 'portuguese', 'english', 'spanish'.
Request body fields (JSON):
  • userAgent – Required. Must be a non-empty string.
  • ip – Required. String, min 7 / max 45 characters (IPv4 or IPv6 address of the client).
  • email – Required. Valid email address. Min 7, max 100 characters.
  • language – Required. Accepted values: 'portuguese', 'english', 'spanish'.

400.description: Invalid email format. The frontend should display a generic system error.

404.description: Email not registered. The frontend should redirect the user to the email confirmation screen.

202.description: Token sent to user's email. The frontend should redirect the user to the password registration screen.

200.description: Password already registered, user has no pending registrations. The frontend should redirect the user to the password entry screen.

403.description: Token is locked. The frontend should redirect the user to the token unlock request screen.

201.description: Pre-registration is pending. The frontend should redirect the user to the pre-registration screen.

post.description:
When does it occur? Right after the system detects missing pre-registration data during the login flow. What does it do? Records the user's onboarding questionnaire answers.

Request body fields (JSON):
  • userAgent – Required. Must be a non-empty string.
  • ip – Required. String, min 7 / max 45 characters (IPv4 or IPv6 address of the client).
  • email – Required. Valid email address. Min 7, max 100 characters.
  • channel – Required. Accepted values: 'linkedin', 'telegram', 'friends', 'others'.
  • goal – Required. Accepted values: 'jobs', 'recruiting'.

400.description: Invalid email format. The frontend should display a generic system error.

404.description: Email not found. The frontend should redirect the user to the email confirmation screen.

200.description: Answers saved, user has no pending registrations. The frontend should redirect the user to the password entry screen.

409.description: User already logged in. The frontend should redirect the user to the password change screen.

403.description: Token is locked. The frontend should redirect the user to the token unlock request screen.

202.description: Password registration is pending. The frontend should redirect the user to the password registration screen.

423.description: Password pending unlock. The frontend should redirect the user to the password change screen.

post.description:
When does it occur? After the system detects a locked or missing password, or when the user wants to change their password. What does it do? Registers the user's access password using a valid one-time token sent by email. The optional query parameter wordsHash can be sent to avoid re-downloading the full word list; if the hash matches, the word list is not returned.

Request body fields (JSON):
  • userAgent – Required. Must be a non-empty string.
  • ip – Required. String, min 7 / max 45 characters (IPv4 or IPv6 address of the client).
  • email – Required. Valid email address. Min 7, max 100 characters.
  • password – Required. Strong password: minimum 8 characters, at least 1 uppercase letter, 1 lowercase letter, 1 digit, and 1 special character.
  • token – Optional. The one-time token sent by email. Must be a non-empty string if provided.

400.description: Invalid email format. The frontend should display a generic system error.

404.description: Email not found. The frontend should redirect the user to the email confirmation screen.

429.description: Token just locked — maximum wrong attempts exceeded. The frontend should redirect the user to the token resend screen.

200.description: Password saved, user has no pending registrations. The frontend should redirect the user to the password entry screen.

423.description: Weak password: the submitted password does not meet strong-password requirements. The frontend should redirect the user to the weak password confirmation screen.

201.description: Pre-registration is pending. The frontend should redirect the user to the pre-registration screen.

403.description: Token is locked. The frontend should redirect the user to the token unlock request screen.

427.description: Wrong token entered. Still within the allowed attempt limit. The frontend should display an error with the remaining attempt count.

get.description:
When does it occur? When the frontend needs to confirm that an existing session is still active. What does it do? Verifies the combination of email (path) + session token against the active session registry.

Path variables:
  • email – Required. Valid email address. Format: ^[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$. Min 7, max 100 characters.
  • sessionToken – Required. Must be exactly 8 characters.

400.description: Invalid email format. The frontend should display a generic system error.

401.description: Session token is invalid or expired.

delete.description:
When does it occur? When the user intentionally ends their session or the frontend needs to disassociate from it. What does it do? Removes the active session so subsequent authenticated requests are rejected.

Path variables:
  • sessionToken – Required. Must be exactly 8 characters.
Request body fields (JSON):
  • userAgent – Required. Must be a non-empty string.
  • ip – Required. String, min 7 / max 45 characters (IPv4 or IPv6 address of the client).
  • email – Required. Valid email address. Min 7, max 100 characters.
  • token – Required. The session token to invalidate.

400.description: Invalid email format. The frontend should display a generic system error.

200.description: Logout executed successfully. The frontend should close the login modal.

404.description: User is not logged in. The frontend should close the login modal.

get.summary: Get async task status by ID
get.description:
When does it occur? When the frontend needs to check the result of a previously triggered background operation. What does it do? Retrieves the current status and result of the async task identified by the given ID.

Path variables:
  • asyncTaskId – Required. The unique identifier of the async task.

200.description: Async task found. The response body contains the task result.

404.description: Async task not found — the ID does not match any known background operation.
